tasks.eng6-newspaper-article: Topic: Writing a newspaper article (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover the headline, by-line, the lead paragraph, the five Ws, facts versus opinion, quotations, the third person and the past tense. Ask questions directly to 'you' in everyday school situations.
tasks.eng6-folklore-myth-legend: Topic: Folklore, myths and legends (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover the difference between a myth and a legend, the features of folklore (simple plot, clear characters, repetition, exaggeration, a lesson), planning and writing a short folktale in the past tense. Use original stories only. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-instructional-text: Topic: Instructional texts: recipes and directions (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover the parts of a recipe, command verbs, sequence words, measurements, warnings, giving directions with landmarks, and testing instructions. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-information-text-weather: Topic: Information texts: weather reports and charts (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover reading a weather chart, units (degrees Celsius, millimetres), the high and low temperature, writing a short weather report in the present and future tense, and facts versus opinion. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-story-writing-plot: Topic: Writing a story with a plot (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover characters, setting, plot, the problem and ending, a plot flow chart, past tense, dialogue with inverted commas, paragraphs and revising. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-character-sketch: Topic: Writing a character sketch (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover appearance and personality, showing with actions rather than telling, exact adjectives and strong verbs, paragraph organisation, third person and consistent tense. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-diary-entry: Topic: Writing a diary entry (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover the date, first person, past tense for events, feelings with reasons, an informal voice and a plan for tomorrow. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-comic-strip-script: Topic: Comic strips and writing a comic script (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover panels, speech and thought bubbles, captions, sound words, planning four to six panels, and a script with panel numbers, picture descriptions and speaker names. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.eng6-descriptive-paragraph: Topic: Writing a descriptive paragraph (Grade 6 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover the topic sentence, the five senses, exact adjectives, strong verbs, similes, tense, and keeping every sentence on the topic. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
